slot.brief: From percentage composition of C, H and O, determine empirical formula and then molecular formula from molar mass.

stem: A compound contains $40\%$ carbon, $6\dfrac{2}{3}\%$ hydrogen and $53\dfrac{1}{3}\%$ oxygen by mass. If its molar mass is $120\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, what is its molecular formula? Use atomic masses C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16.

verdicts.working: For 100 g: C:H:O mole ratio = 40/12 : 6.667/1 : 53.333/16 = 1:2:1, giving empirical formula CH₂O (30 g mol⁻¹). The molecular mass is 120 g mol⁻¹, so multiply the empirical formula by 4: C₄H₈O₄.

working:
For $100\ \text{g}$: $n_{\text{C}}:n_{\text{H}}:n_{\text{O}}=\dfrac{40}{12}:\dfrac{20}{3}:\dfrac{160/3}{16}=1:2:1$. Empirical formula $=\text{CH}_2\text{O}$; empirical formula mass $=30\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. Multiplying factor $=\dfrac{120}{30}=4$. Molecular formula $=\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_4$.

Independent check: For 100 g: C:H:O mole ratio = 40/12 : 6.667/1 : 53.333/16 = 1:2:1, giving empirical formula CH₂O (30 g mol⁻¹). The molecular mass is 120 g mol⁻¹, so multiply the empirical formula by 4: C₄H₈O₄.
